data.answer: This returns up to five class symbol identifiers together with the number of methods defined directly on each class. A method is associated with a class when both symbols come from the same file and the method's qualified name is exactly the class qualified name, a dot, and the method's bare name. The results are grouped by class symbol identifier, ordered by method count from highest to lowest, and then by class symbol identifier ascending to break ties.

display_annotations.note: Deterministic display links; not source citations made by the model.

output_contract.guidance: Count only methods defined directly on each class. Return the class symbol ID and method count. Order by methods descending, then symbol_id ascending.

data.question: Which classes define the most methods? Give the top five.
data.reference_sql:
SELECT c.symbol_id, COUNT(*) AS methods
FROM code.symbols c
JOIN code.symbols m ON m.file_id = c.file_id AND m.kind = 'method'
  AND m.qualname = c.qualname || '.' || m.name
WHERE c.kind = 'class'
GROUP BY c.symbol_id
ORDER BY methods DESC, c.symbol_id
LIMIT 5;

request.evidence: A method's qualname is its class's qualname followed by a dot and the method name.
request.question:
Which classes define the most methods? Give the top five.

Requested output columns: symbol_id (string), methods (integer).
Return every requested field using exactly its specified column alias. Preserve complete case-sensitive repository-relative paths and symbol IDs; do not substitute display names. Include all requested counts and provenance fields. Explain the query result in ordinary prose; do not emit placeholder text. These questions concern a static map of open-source Python code. After executing SQL, describe the returned rows and query assumptions. Questions asking which files, modules or symbols mean distinct identities, not one repeated row per matching import or call occurrence; preserve occurrence counts only when requested. Caller/callee graph questions include methods as well as standalone functions unless a symbol kind is explicitly restricted. Use files.is_test for test-file classification; test_links describe associations, not the complete set of test files. Use DOUBLE or DECIMAL, rather than single-precision REAL, for percentage calculations.
Count only methods defined directly on each class. Return the class symbol ID and method count. Order by methods descending, then symbol_id ascending.

data.sql:
SELECT c.symbol_id, COUNT(m.symbol_id) AS methods
FROM auto_ontology_code.code.symbols AS c
JOIN auto_ontology_code.code.symbols AS m
  ON c.kind = 'class'
 AND m.kind = 'method'
 AND c.file_id = m.file_id
 AND m.qualname = c.qualname || '.' || m.name
GROUP BY c.symbol_id
ORDER BY methods DESC, c.symbol_id ASC
LIMIT 5;
